title: MSA §5.3 vendor-disclosure authority and monitoring
summary:
Asked about the interaction between MSA §5.3 (Flock's authority to disclose customer data 'as required to provide services') and Civil Code §1798.90.55(b) (which addresses agency authorization for ALPR-information sharing).

The request covered SMPD authorizations of any §5.3 disclosures, records of how the Department would learn of one if it occurred, and the City's legal analysis of the two provisions read together.

policy_promises.quote: ALPR information shall not be sold, shared, or transferred except to another public agency, and only as otherwise permitted by law
policy_promises.tests: What records document SMPD's authorization of any Flock-initiated disclosure under §5.3?

policy_promises.quote: Flock may disclose Customer Data as required to provide the Services
policy_promises.tests: What SMPD records describe monitoring of, or limits on, Flock's §5.3 disclosure authority?

prior_pra_refs.note: W012174 returned 'no records responsive' for external-agency access records (Feb 2026). This request's rolling production surfaced Flock camera-access-request emails in SMPD inboxes — records bearing on that earlier request that were not identified as responsive to it.

filed_because: Surfacing how SMPD documents authorization, monitoring, and legal analysis of the vendor-disclosure clause in its Flock contract.
notes:
Item 4 (legal analysis) was denied 2026-03-13 citing attorney-client privilege.

The request was closed on 2026-05-06 by consolidation into W012462-040226 (an email-only corpus). The original request scope included legal analysis, monitoring records, and authorizations that fall outside an inbound-email search.

Follow-ups W012683-050626 (Item 6 isolated) and W012686-050726 (broader re-filing) re-asked the substantive questions after W012462 was withdrawn.
